text_blocks.snippet: High blood pressure (hypertension) usually causes no symptoms or warning signs, which is why it is often called the "silent killer". The only reliable way to know your numbers is to measure your blood pressure.
When Symptoms Appear (Severe Spikes or Crisis)
If your blood pressure becomes extremely high or reaches a dangerous crisis level (above 180/120 mm Hg), you may notice physical warning signs:

list.snippet: Severe headaches: Throbbing or intense head pain, often starting in the morning.
Vision changes: Blurry vision, double vision, or eye strain from strained blood vessels in the eyes.
Shortness of breath: Difficulty catching your breath during light activity or at rest.
Chest pain: Tightness, pressure, or a squeezing sensation in the chest.
Dizziness or fatigue: Feeling lightheaded, woozy, or unusually exhausted.
Nosebleeds: Spontaneous or frequent nosebleeds from delicate nasal blood vessels under pressure.
Heart palpitations: A racing, pounding, or irregular heartbeat.
Confusion: Sudden trouble concentrating or mental fog.

text_blocks.snippet: Blood pressure readings above 180/120 mm Hg paired with symptoms like chest pain, shortness of breath, back pain, numbness, weakness, change in vision, or difficulty speaking signal a hypertensive emergency. Get emergency medical help right away.
Learn more about the condition and guidelines at the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention and review detailed risk factors with the American Heart Association.
